raw_response:
The silver step derives txn_date from ingest_ts, which is the delivery time, not the transaction time. The change on 2026-01-16 (DE-398) most likely introduced this. The alert counts 4699 rows, which equals all POSTED rows, so every row mismatches. Each batch is ingested at 02:00 the day after the transactions, so ingest date is always txn date + 1.

The fix is to derive txn_date from txn_ts: CAST(txn_ts AS DATE).

The evidence is consistent. Sample batches 11 through 14 each show txn_ts one day before ingest_ts, and the monitor defines consistency as txn_date equal to the date of txn_ts. The min txn_ts is 2026-01-05 and the min ingest_ts is 2026-01-06, which matches the one-day offset. No other issues are visible, such as duplicates (txn_id is distinct) or join key problems. The REVERSED filter is presumably intended and I leave it unchanged. The gold tables rebuild from silver, so only the silver step needs replacing.

{"diagnosis":"silver_transactions derives txn_date from ingest_ts (delivery time, always the day after the transaction) instead of txn_ts, so every row's txn_date is off by one day versus the date of txn_ts; gold tables inherit the wrong dates.","decision":"fix","confidence":0.93,"pre_sql":[],"step_overrides":{"silver_transactions":"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
